history.period: 19th century (samadhi dated 1850 CE on official site; conflicts noted)
history.summary: FLAG - identity ambiguity: this is not an independent temple but the Samadhi Sthal (samadhi shrine) of Bhakt Shiromani Mohandas Ji Maharaj - the founder-devotee who installed the Salasar Balaji idol in 1754 - together with his sister Kanhi Dadi Ji, located inside the Salasar Balaji Dham complex at Salasar. CSV's 'Kanidadi' is rendered here as Kanhi Dadi Ji (also called Kanhi Bai); CSV's 'Mohan Das Ji' is Mohandas Ji Maharaj. Before taking jeevit samadhi on Vaishakh Shukla Triyodashi, Mohandas Ji appointed his nephew Udayaram Ji as first priest and asked Balaji's blessings for the priestly lineage; the memorial inscription was raised by Udayaram Ji in 1852. His taposthali (dhuna) stands at the temple's south gate, where the Akhand Dhuni has burned since the temple's inception. FLAG: the official site dates the samadhi to 1850 CE, while its history page says 1794 (Baisakh Shukla Trayodashi) - source dates conflict; document as uncertain.

name: Mohan Das Ji & Kanidadi Shrine
town_description: Salasar is a pilgrim town in Sujangarh tehsil of Churu district, Rajasthan, on the Jaipur-Bikaner National Highway 65. The town's identity and economy revolve around the Balaji temple complex, inside which this samadhi shrine stands.
tradition: Saint veneration (samadhi sthal of a Hanuman devotee-saint, within the Balaji temple complex)

travel.railway: Sujangarh (~24 km, verify); Sikar (~57 km, verify)
travel.road: Same as Salasar Balaji - inside the temple complex on Balaji Temple Road

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Vaishakh Shukla Trayodashi for the samadhi-day observance
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily ~4:00 AM-10:00 PM, as part of the Balaji temple complex (verify locally)
